stem:
The halogens chlorine, bromine and iodine show trends in chemical and physical properties down the group.

Table 3.1 shows some properties of chlorine, bromine and iodine.

Table 3.1

| property | chlorine | bromine | iodine |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| colour and state at room temperature | green gas |  |  |
| bond energy / $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ | 242 | 193 | 151 |
| electronegativity | 3.0 | 2.8 | 2.5 |
| formula of sodium halide | $\text{NaCl}$ | $\text{NaBr}$ | $\text{NaI}$ |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The bond energy values in Table 3.1 refer to the $\text{X}-\text{X}$ bond where X is the halogen.

Explain the trend in the bond strength of the $\text{X}-\text{X}$ bond in the halogens.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain, with the use of an equation, how chlorine, $\text{Cl}_2$, is used in water purification. State the role of the active species produced.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: The sodium halides in Table 3.1 also show trends in chemical properties.
parts.text: Identify the sodium halide that reacts with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form $\text{H}_2\text{S}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the sodium halide that only undergoes a Brønsted-Lowry acid-base reaction with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: A student adds a few drops of $\text{AgNO}_3\text{(aq)}$ to a solution of $\text{NaBr}\text{(aq)}$. State what is observed.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
Iodine monobromide, $\text{IBr}$, is a dark red solid that melts near room temperature.

$\text{IBr}$ reacts with propene. The mechanism for this reaction is the same as the mechanism for that of $\text{HBr}$ with propene.
parts.text: Identify all the intermolecular forces that exist between molecules of $\text{IBr}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Name the mechanism involved in the reaction of $\text{IBr}$ with propene.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
The reaction of $\text{IBr}$ with propene forms two structural isomers.

Draw the two structural isomers shown by these molecules.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text: Identify the type of structural isomerism shown by the molecules in (d)(iii).

parts.label: (d)(v)
parts.text: Explain why the two structural isomers do not form in equal amounts.
